title: Rollout latency simulation mode — prototype & stakeholder feedback
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Ship an interactive prototype in the Console Rollouts inspector that lets PMs and SREs preview how a rollout behaves under degraded network conditions or higher token latencies. The feature — 'Latency Simulation Mode' — overlays synthetic latency on requests and visualizes fallback behavior (model fallback, regional fallback, retry/backoff) across the rollout timeline and canary cohorts.

Why: During on-call drills and internal launch reviews teams have asked for a deterministic way to preview service degradation and confirm that rollout safety policies (rollbacks, rate-limits, automatic fallback) visually and operationally behave as expected before a rollout hits prod. This prototype is meant to reduce surprises in enterprise Dedicated/Private deployments where network variability is more common.

Scope of this ticket: build high-fidelity Figma prototype and interactive InVision/ProtoFlow playback that demonstrates: 1) a toggle to enable Latency Simulation Mode, 2) slider controls for simulated median p95 latency and packet loss, 3) timeline playback that animates request traces across cohorts with synthetic latency applied, 4) visual badges for safety actions (canary paused, automated region failover, model downgrade), and 5) a short QA script and acceptance criteria for dev handoff.

Design decisions / trade-offs considered:
- Visual density vs. clarity: we intentionally moved non-essential metrics (CPU/GPU utilization) into an expandable sidecar to keep main timeline readable.
- Live metrics vs. synthetic playback: prototype supports both live-synced playback and fully deterministic simulated runs; for first pass we prioritize deterministic playback to make reviews reproducible.
- Interaction affordance: simulation controls are modal to avoid accidental toggles during active rollouts; team requested an opt-in persisted user preference.

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma prototype includes 3 simulation presets (light jitter, moderate latency, network outage) and custom sliders.
- Playback visually annotates when a fallback triggers and shows the cohort affected.
- Developer handoff includes a single-page spec with CSS/animation guidance, list of telemetry flags required, and the QA script.
- Stakeholder alignment: PM + Infra lead + two SRE reviewers sign off in comments.

Deliverables and links:
- Figma file: https://figma.com/file/REPLACE_ME/rollout-latency-sim (frame names: Prototype / Playback / Controls)
- ProtoFlow playback: https://protflow.company/plays/rollout-latency-sim (internal)
- Handoff doc (Drive): https://drive.company/drive/rollout-latency-handoff (includes QA, telemetry list, flag names)
- Implementation tickets: ENG-3312 (backend simulation support), ENG-3499 (UI integration & animation)

qa_script:
Steps:
1) Open Console > Rollouts > select active rollout > open inspector.
2) Toggle 'Latency Simulation Mode' (persisted opt-in) — confirm audit log entry emitted.
3) Select 'Moderate latency' preset. Hit Play.
4) Verify timeline animates and displays safety badges (canary pause, fallback).
5) Resize viewport to 320px width and confirm labels wrap and no overlap.
6) Enable 'packet loss' slider at 10% and confirm cohort failure state is visualized.
7) Capture screenshots for each preset and attach to ticket.
Expected: deterministic, reproducible playback; badges readable at AA contrast; simulation does not mutate live rollout state (read-only simulation).
handoff_notes: Developer handoff must include: list of telemetry flags (sim_mode_enabled, sim_preset, sim_params), recommended CSS animation durations (200ms ease-out for badge fade, 400ms for timeline scrub), accessibility changes (aria-live region for playback state), and mock trace payloads for deterministic playback tests.
